title: Exercise 7A · Q2(d)
summary: Find the shorter side d from the hypotenuse 24.7 m and the other side 14.5 m.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q2(d): Find the value of the unknown d. The hypotenuse is 24.7 m and the right angle is between the 14.5 m side and the side d.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: The hypotenuse is **24.7 m** and one shorter side is **14.5 m**. The right angle is between the **14.5 m** side and the unknown side **d**. We have to find **d**.

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In the right-angled triangle, the right angle is at **R**. The **hypotenuse** is the side opposite the right angle — the longest side.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{\text{hypotenuse}^2} &= \role{legA}{\text{leg}^2} + \role{legB}{\text{leg}^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length. The unknown side stays as a letter.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{\text{hypotenuse}^2} &= \role{legA}{\text{leg}^2} + \role{legB}{\text{leg}^2} \\ \role{hyp}{24.7^2} &= \role{legA}{d^2} + \role{legB}{14.5^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Make the unknown the subject
steps.narration: We want a **shorter side**, so subtract the known square from the hypotenuse square.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{\text{hypotenuse}^2} &= \role{legA}{\text{leg}^2} + \role{legB}{\text{leg}^2} \\ \role{hyp}{24.7^2} &= \role{legA}{d^2} + \role{legB}{14.5^2} \\ \role{legA}{d^2} &= \role{hyp}{24.7^2} - \role{legB}{14.5^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 399.84 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{\text{hypotenuse}^2} &= \role{legA}{\text{leg}^2} + \role{legB}{\text{leg}^2} \\ \role{hyp}{24.7^2} &= \role{legA}{d^2} + \role{legB}{14.5^2} \\ \role{legA}{d^2} &= \role{hyp}{24.7^2} - \role{legB}{14.5^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{610.09} - \role{legB}{210.25} \\ &= \role{legA}{399.84} \\ \role{legA}{d} &= \sqrt{399.84} = \role{ans}{20.0\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse **26 m** and one shorter side **10 m**. Find the other shorter side.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find a shorter side: **subtract** the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the **square root**.
A shorter side must be **smaller** than the hypotenuse — a quick check on your answer.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
